questions.question: Write one advantage of using biofertilizers over chemical fertilizers. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write one advantage of using biofertilizers over chemical fertilizers. [U] / [CO4]
  • Biofertilizers enhance soil health by increasing microbial diversity and improving soil
  • structure, thereby promoting long-term soil fertility and sustainability without causing
  • pollution or soil degradation.

questions.question: What is the composition of Bacterial cell membrane? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the composition of Bacterial cell membrane? [ K] / [CO1]
  • The membrane is composed of a fluid phospholipid bilayer (40%). Proteins constitute about 60% of
  • the bacterial membrane. Many bacteria contain hopanoids, sterol -like molecules that stabilize the
  • membrane structure.

questions.question: What is transformation in bacteria? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is transformation in bacteria? [U] / [CO2]
  • Transformation in bacteria is the process by which bacteria take up free, foreign DNA from their
  • surroundings and incorporate it into their own genetic material. This results in a change in the bacterial
  • genetic constitution, allowing the expression of new traits such as antibiotic resistance or the ability to
  • utilize different nutrients.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why is Gram’s staining important in microbiology? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is Gram’s staining important in microbiology? [U] / [CO3]
  • Gram staining allows for the rapid classification of bacteria into two major groups, Gram-
  • positive and Gram -negative, based on their cell wall composition. This differentiation
  • facilitates the identification and diagnosis of bacterial infections, thereby guiding the
  • selection of appropriate antibiotic treatments.

questions.question: What are anaerobic bacteria? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What are anaerobic bacteria? [U] / [CO2]
  • Anaerobic bacteria are microorganisms that can survive and grow in environments with little or
  • no oxygen. They do not require oxygen for their metabolism and produce energy through
  • fermentation or anaerobic respiration.

questions.question: What is a cloning vector? / [CO2] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• What is a cloning vector? [U] / [CO2]
  • A cloning vector is a small piece of DNA, such as a plasmid or virus, used in molecular biology to carry a
  • foreign DNA fragment into a host cell where it can be replicated and/or expressed. The vector contains
  • essential features, such as an origin of replication for autonomous replication, a multiple cloning site for
  • inserting foreign DNA, and a selectable marker gene (often antibiotic resistance) to identify cells carrying
  • the recombinant DNA.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Outline the process of conjugation in bacteria. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define the process of conjugation in bacteria. [K] / [CO2]
  • Bacterial conjugation is a process of genetic material transfer between bacterial cells through
  • direct contact. The donor bacterium (F+ cell) forms a sex pilus, a tube -like structure, to connect to the
  • recipient cell (F - cell). The pilus draws the recipient close to the donor, forming a conjugation bridge
  • between their cytoplasm. A plasmid DNA in the donor is nicked by an enzyme at the origin of transfer
  • (oriT). A single strand of plasmid DNA is transferred to the recipient cell through the pilus in the 5’ to 3’
  • direction. Both donor and recipient synthesize the complementary DNA strand to restore double-stranded
  • plasmids; the recipient becomes capable of acting as a donor in future conjugations.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write short notes on endospores. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write short notes on endospores. [K] / [CO2]
  • Endospores are dormant, tough, and highly resistant structures formed by certain Gram -positive bacteria,
  • such as Bacillus and Clostridium, in response to unfavorable environmental conditions. They enable bacteria
  • to survive extreme stresses, including heat, desiccation, chemicals, and radiation.

questions.question: Write a brief note on culture media used in microbiology. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a brief note on culture media used in microbiology. [U] / [CO3]
  • Culture media in microbiology are nutrient-rich substances used to support the growth, isolation, and
  • identification of microorganisms in vitro. They provide the essential nutrients, moisture, and
  • environmental conditions needed for microbial proliferation.Basal (Basic) Media, Enriched Media,
  • Selective Media, Differential/Indicator Media, Enrichment Media, Transport Media, Storage Media.
  • Physical forms include liquid (broth), solid (agar plates), and semi-solid media, each suited for different
  • laboratory applications, such as cultivation, isolation, or motility testing. (Any 5 types).
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a brief note on bioremediation. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a brief note on bioremediation [U][CO4]
  • Bioremediation is an eco -friendly process that utilizes living organisms, such as bacteria, fungi,
  • or plants, to degrade, de toxify, or remove pollutants and contaminants from the environment,
  • including soil, water, and air. The organisms metabolize the harmful substances, converting them
  • into less toxic or harmless products, such as water, carbon dioxide, and biomass. Bioremediation
  • can be performed in situ (at the site of contamination ) or ex situ (removal and treatment
  • elsewhere). This technique is widely used to clean oil spills, pesticides, heavy metals, and other
  • industrial pollutants, promoting environmental sustainability and reducing chemical waste.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
